content.directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence "Living in an increasingly competitive world, college students should better prepare themselves to confront various challenges." You can make comments, cite examples or use your personal experiences to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
content.topic: College students confronting challenges in a competitive world

model_essay.title: Preparing for Challenges in a Competitive World
model_essay.content:
Living in an increasingly competitive world, college students should better prepare themselves to confront various challenges. The rapid pace of technological advancement and economic globalization has intensified competition in almost every field, making it imperative for students to equip themselves with both knowledge and practical skills.

First and foremost, students should cultivate a habit of lifelong learning. Academic excellence alone is no longer sufficient; one must constantly update knowledge and acquire new competencies to remain relevant in the job market. Additionally, developing strong interpersonal and communication skills is equally essential, as teamwork and collaboration have become indispensable in modern workplaces.

Moreover, college students ought to build psychological resilience. Setbacks and failures are inevitable, and the ability to bounce back from adversity distinguishes successful individuals from others. Engaging in extracurricular activities, internships, and volunteer work can help students gain real-world experience and strengthen their adaptability.

In conclusion, by embracing continuous learning, honing social skills, and fostering mental toughness, college students can confidently navigate the challenges that lie ahead.

structure_analysis.opening: 开篇以题目要求的首句引入话题，指出当今世界竞争加剧的背景，强调大学生做好准备的必要性。
structure_analysis.body: 主体段分两个层次展开：第一层从知识技能角度出发，强调终身学习和人际沟通能力的重要性；第二层从心理素质角度出发，论述抗压能力和实践经验对应对挑战的关键作用。论证逻辑清晰，层层递进。
structure_analysis.closing: 结尾总结全文，重申持续学习、社交能力和心理韧性三个要点，呼应开头，首尾呼应，结构完整。

highlights: 使用高级过渡词语（First and foremost, Additionally, Moreover, In conclusion）使文章逻辑衔接自然流畅
运用现在分词短语作状语（Living in...）和独立主格结构，展现高级句式驾驭能力
词汇选用精准且多样化，如 imperative、indispensable、resilience、adaptability 等六级高频词汇，避免词汇重复
论证方式多样，将抽象论点与具体建议（如实习、志愿活动）相结合，增强说服力

transcript.text: What can you tell us?

transcript.speaker: M

transcript.text: One thing I've learned in a quarter century of management is that there are ample grey areas in human behaviour, and that there may not always be clear right or wrong solutions to employee disputes.
transcript.translation: 在管理岗位上工作二十五年，我学到的一点是，人类行为中存在许多灰色地带，员工纠纷的解决方案并非总是清晰的是非对错。

transcript.text: When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe.
transcript.translation: 当两个人对同一事件有不同版本时，很难知道该相信谁。

transcript.text: One such circumstance always comes back to me.
transcript.translation: 有一件事总是让我想起。

transcript.text: It happened years ago, and it's a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution.
transcript.translation: 那是多年前的事了，这场冲突如此不值得记忆，以至于我甚至记不清纠纷的具体内容，但我绝对记得解决方案。

transcript.text: Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event, and it seemed likely we'd never get to the truth.
transcript.translation: 两位有才华的年轻高管，其中一位由我管理，对同一事件有截然不同的说法，看来我们永远无法得知真相。

transcript.text: We reached a deadlock, and the manager of the other individual said, Here's something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for.
transcript.translation: 我们陷入了僵局，另一位高管的经理说：“这是我从一位我曾经共事的优秀经理那里学到的。”

transcript.text: He used to say, And just like that, we had a path forward.
transcript.translation: 他过去常说，就这样，我们找到了前进的道路。

transcript.text: My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter.
transcript.translation: 我和我的同事一致认为，我们可能永远无法查明事情的真相。

transcript.text: Quite likely, there were elements of truth in both employees' stories.
transcript.translation: 很可能，两位员工的故事中都有真实的成分。

transcript.text: We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further.
transcript.translation: 我们同意今后监控他们的行动和关系，但不再进一步干预。

transcript.text: We assumed the best about both of them and moved on.
transcript.translation: 我们对双方都做了最善意的假设，然后继续前进。

transcript.text: The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us.
transcript.translation: 结果是，我们能够将冲突抛在脑后。

transcript.text: In fact, their problems didn't recur.
transcript.translation: 事实上，他们的问题没有再次发生。

transcript.text: Over the years, this general approach has proved useful.
transcript.translation: 多年来，这种通用方法被证明是有效的。

transcript.text: Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision.
transcript.translation: 每当真相不明时，假设积极意图并同意继续前进可能是一个建设性的决定。

transcript.text: For some Americans, going out to dinner is a treat, planned and budgeted for.
transcript.translation: 对一些美国人来说，外出就餐是一种享受，需要计划和预算。

transcript.text: For others, it's just a daily occurrence.
transcript.translation: 对另一些人来说，这只是一个日常事件。

transcript.text: And that second group of people is becoming the majority, as the number of Americans who enjoy cooking is declining.
transcript.translation: 而第二组人正在成为多数，因为喜欢烹饪的美国人数量在减少。

transcript.text: In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans' attitudes to cooking.
transcript.translation: 在21世纪初，研究员Eddie Yoon进行了一项调查，以确定美国人对烹饪的态度。

transcript.text: The survey found that 15% of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook, and 35% reported mixed feelings.
transcript.translation: 调查发现，15%的美国人热爱烹饪，50%的人表示讨厌烹饪，35%的人报告有复杂感受。

transcript.text: When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it, and 45% had mixed feelings.
transcript.translation: 当Yoon在15年后进行相同调查时，只有10%的受访者表示热爱烹饪，45%的人表示讨厌它，45%的人有复杂感受。

transcript.text: Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing.
transcript.translation: Yoon断言烹饪类似于缝纫。

transcript.text: As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing.
transcript.translation: 就在20世纪初，许多美国人自己缝制衣服。

transcript.text: Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing.
transcript.translation: 如今，绝大多数美国人购买衣服。

transcript.text: Only a tiny minority still sew, and they do it mainly as a hobby.
transcript.translation: 只有极少数人仍然缝纫，而且他们主要是作为爱好来做。

transcript.text: Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion.
transcript.translation: Yoon相信家庭厨师的数量将以类似方式减少。

transcript.text: Currently, the average American household spends over $3 ,000 per year on dining out.
transcript.translation: 目前，美国家庭平均每年在外出就餐上花费超过3000美元。

transcript.text: However, what people save in convenience, they lose in cash.
transcript.translation: 然而，人们在便利上节省的，在现金上却损失了。

transcript.text: Take buying lunch on work days, for example.
transcript.translation: 以工作日买午餐为例。

transcript.text: People spend, on average, $10 per meal when they buy lunch.
transcript.translation: 当人们买午餐时，平均每餐花费10美元。

transcript.text: Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less.
transcript.translation: 与此同时，自己做午餐会花费更少。

transcript.text: One survey found people only spend, on average, $6.
transcript.translation: 一项调查发现，人们平均每餐只花费6美元。

transcript.text: 30 when they bring lunch prepared at home.
transcript.translation: 当他们带家里准备的午餐时，只花费30。

transcript.text: Americans' growing aversion to spending time in the kitchen signifies a host of challenges for the grocery industry.
transcript.translation: 美国人对在厨房花时间的日益厌恶标志着杂货行业面临的一系列挑战。

transcript.text: It's likely to detrimentally impact family finances as well.
transcript.translation: 这也可能对家庭财务产生不利影响。

transcript.text: 5 billion bags checked onto flights worldwide, 26 million go missing.
transcript.translation: 5亿个行李箱被托运行李，其中2600万个丢失。

transcript.text: And of that 26 million, 1 million never make it back to their original owner.
transcript.translation: 在这2600万个中，有100万个从未归还原主。

transcript.text: Bad weather and flight delays, miscoded destination tags, and some people simply forgetting to pick up one of their bags are a few of the reasons.
transcript.translation: 恶劣天气和航班延误、目的地标签编码错误，以及一些人 simply 忘记取走自己的行李箱，是其中几个原因。

transcript.text: But the number one reason a bag ends up lost is that it has no ID tag and airlines don't know to whom it belongs.
transcript.translation: 但行李箱丢失的首要原因是它没有身份标签，航空公司不知道它属于谁。

transcript.text: Transferring baggage from check-in to departure gates, to arrival gates, to baggage claim is a delicate piece of timing.
transcript.translation: 将行李箱从值机处转运到登机口、到达口、再到行李认领处，是一项时机精妙的工作。

transcript.text: If the system moves too slowly, the bags won't make connecting flights.
transcript.translation: 如果系统移动太慢，行李箱就赶不上转机航班。

transcript.text: If it's too fast, the bags may make the connection, but the passengers might miss the flight.
transcript.translation: 如果它太快，行李箱可能赶上转机，但乘客可能会错过航班。

transcript.text: Each airport has its own way of allotting how much time a bag needs to move in transit.
transcript.translation: 每个机场都有自己分配行李箱在转运中所需时间的方式。

transcript.text: Some airports have sophisticated automated systems, including scanners that read baggage labels, destination coded vehicles that load and unload the bags without stopping, and sorting machines that route baggage to the appropriate gate.
transcript.translation: 一些机场拥有先进的自动化系统，包括读取行李标签的扫描仪、无需停靠即可装卸行李的目的地编码车辆，以及将行李路由到适当登机口的分拣机。

transcript.text: Even so, all that technology may not save your baggage tag from being torn off on the conveyor belt, making you the owner of a bag with no name.
transcript.translation: 即便如此，所有这些技术可能无法防止你的行李标签在传送带上被撕掉，使你成为没有名字的行李箱的主人。

transcript.text: Once a bag goes missing and the passenger files a claim, the bag is declared mishandled by the carrier.
transcript.translation: 一旦行李箱丢失，乘客提出索赔，该行李箱就被承运商宣布为处理不当。

transcript.text: Mishandled refers to bags that have been delayed, lost, stolen or damaged.
transcript.translation: 处理不当指的是被延误、丢失、偷窃或损坏的行李箱。

transcript.text: Most delayed bags are only one flight behind their owners and can be delivered within 24 hours.
transcript.translation: 大多数延误的行李箱只比主人晚一个航班，可以在24小时内送达。

transcript.text: The other bags are examined by airline employees for clues to their ownership and destination.
transcript.translation: 其他行李箱由航空公司员工检查，以寻找其所有权和目的地的线索。

transcript.text: If the mystery is solved, those bags are returned to their owners within four or five days.
transcript.translation: 如果谜团解开，那些行李箱会在四五天内归还给主人。

transcript.text: Bags with no destination code or identification tag are shipped to a central warehouse and undergo a comprehensive baggage tracing process over the next 90 days.
transcript.translation: 没有目的地代码或身份标签的行李箱被运送到中央仓库，并在接下来的90天内经历全面的行李追踪过程。

transcript.text: Airlines inventory their mishandled baggage, and many use a database to match the contents with owners' descriptions.
transcript.translation: 航空公司清点其处理不当的行李箱，许多使用数据库将内容与主人的描述匹配。

transcript.text: It takes about three months to go from missing in action to irretrievably lost.
transcript.translation: 从丢失到无法找回的丢失大约需要三个月。

transcript.text: Once that happens, the bags are donated to charity, sold at auction, or purchased by a company which sells them to the public.
transcript.translation: 一旦发生这种情况，行李箱会被捐赠给慈善机构、拍卖，或由公司购买后向公众出售。

transcript.text: So, never pack anything of real value in your checked baggage, and make sure your name is on the bag along with your phone number so an agent can contact you.
transcript.translation: 所以，永远不要在托运行李中打包任何真正有价值的东西，并确保你的名字和电话号码在行李箱上，以便代理人能联系你。

transcript.text: You've probably been with someone who ignored you while interacting with his or her smartphone, and you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself.
transcript.translation: 你可能曾遇到过有人在与你互动时只顾玩手机而忽略你，而且你自己也可能做过类似的事。

transcript.text: In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they'd used their smartphone during their most recent social activity.
transcript.translation: 在最近的一项调查中，十分之九的受访者表示，他们在最近一次社交活动中使用了智能手机。

transcript.text: There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful.
transcript.translation: 还有证据表明，这种行为对社会有害。

transcript.text: It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions, and it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy.
transcript.translation: 这会让人们对面对面的交流感到不那么满意，并可能产生怨恨和嫉妒的情绪。

transcript.text: Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects.
transcript.translation: 现在，《应用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究，探讨这些影响的原因。

transcript.text: The study included 128 mostly female student participants.
transcript.translation: 该研究包括128名以女性为主的学生参与者。

transcript.text: The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation.
transcript.translation: 参与者观看了一个三分钟的动画，其中两个卡通人物互动并进行了对话。

transcript.text: The conversation couldn't be heard, but could be detected through mouth movements.
transcript.translation: 对话无法听到，但可以通过嘴部动作来识别。

transcript.text: Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners.
transcript.translation: 参与者必须想象自己是视频中最接近的人物，然后对对话以及他们对对话伙伴的感受做出判断。

transcript.text: In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participant's conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation.
transcript.translation: 在实验的一个版本中，参与者的对话伙伴的手机在对话过程中一直放在桌上未使用。

transcript.text: In another version, their partner's attention was quickly drawn to something on their phone, and they spent the rest of the time interacting with their phone.
transcript.translation: 在另一个版本中，他们的伙伴的注意力很快被手机上的某物吸引，并在剩余时间里与手机互动。

transcript.text: A third version involved the participant's partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone.
transcript.translation: 第三个版本涉及参与者的伙伴在手机互动和忽视手机的时段之间交替。

transcript.text: If you've experienced a similar situation, you probably won't be surprised by the results of the experiments.
transcript.translation: 如果你经历过类似的情况，你可能不会对实验结果感到惊讶。

transcript.text: The participants had a negative view of phone use during social interactions.
transcript.translation: 参与者对社交互动中的手机使用持负面看法。

transcript.text: The more it was present, the worse they considered both the quality of the interaction and the quality of the relationship.
transcript.translation: 手机出现得越多，他们认为互动质量和关系质量就越差。

transcript.text: The researchers believed that focusing on one's phone instead of the person one is with has this effect because it's seen as a form of social exclusion.
transcript.translation: 研究人员认为，专注于手机而不是身边的人会产生这种效果，因为这被视为一种社会排斥形式。

transcript.text: They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria.
transcript.translation: 他们断言，这种行为类似于人们别无选择只能在学校的自助餐厅独自用餐。

transcript.text: The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation.
transcript.translation: 转折在于，这种排斥发生在共享物理接触和进行对话的同时。

transcript.text: Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning, and self-esteem.
transcript.translation: 研究人员发现，这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊心产生了不利影响。

transcript.text: These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion.
transcript.translation: 这些负面影响类似于传统社会排斥形式所引起的。

transcript.text: The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience.
transcript.translation: 新发现很重要，因为它们详细阐述了我们对日常经验中微妙但常见方面的理解。

transcript.text: This common behavior can create vicious cycles of detachment even as we try to connect with others.
transcript.translation: 这种常见行为即使在我们试图与他人建立联系时，也可能造成疏离的恶性循环。

transcript.text: More and more people travel for a variety of reasons.
transcript.translation: 越来越多的人出于各种原因旅行。

transcript.text: Many are tourists, but many venture forth on personal or professional business.
transcript.translation: 许多是游客，但也有很多人出于个人或公务出差。

transcript.text: Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find.
transcript.translation: 无论旅行的原因是什么，旅行者们的一个常见抱怨是他们找到的住宿缺乏人情味。

transcript.text: After spending five consecutive nights in five similar hotels, the business traveler may find it difficult to remember what happened from day to day, or even what towns were visited.
transcript.translation: 在五个相似的酒店连续住五晚后，商务旅行者可能很难记住每天发生了什么，甚至记不清去了哪些城镇。

transcript.text: And the tourist may get the mistaken impression that all cities are pretty much the same, at least as far as decoration, food and service are concerned.
transcript.translation: 而游客可能会错误地认为所有城市都大同小异，至少在装饰、食物和服务方面是如此。

transcript.text: To combat this sense of impersonal sameness, travelers are taking advantage of in-home hospitality or bed and breakfast arrangements.
transcript.translation: 为了对抗这种缺乏个性的相似感，旅行者们开始利用家庭式款待或住宿加早餐的安排。

transcript.text: B&Bs, I mean bed and breakfast arrangements, are private homes, which offer lodging and breakfast in a very personalised, friendly setting.
transcript.translation: 住宿加早餐安排是私人住宅，在非常个性化、友好的环境中提供住宿和早餐。

transcript.text: For decades, B&Bs have been the classic ways of visit Europe, especially the British Isles, and in fact, they are not really a new idea in America.
transcript.translation: 几十年来，住宿加早餐一直是游览欧洲，尤其是不列颠群岛的经典方式，事实上，它们在美国并不是一个新概念。

transcript.text: The tradition dates back to colonial times, when inns were few and far between, and the weary traveler had to depend on the kindness of strangers for a meal and a bed.
transcript.translation: 这一传统可以追溯到殖民时代，那时旅馆稀少，疲惫的旅行者不得不依靠陌生人的善意来获得一顿饭和一张床。

transcript.text: But the revival of B&Bs as desirable accommodations is a fairly recent phenomenon.
transcript.translation: 但住宿加早餐作为理想住宿的复兴是相当近期的现象。

transcript.text: If the idea of operating a B&B arouses your interest, there are several factors to consider before plunging into this business.
transcript.translation: 如果经营住宿加早餐的想法引起了你的兴趣，那么在投身这一业务之前，有几个因素需要考虑。

transcript.text: The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location.
transcript.translation: 第一个考虑因素是你的房产，不仅是建筑本身，还有位置。

transcript.text: If you live near a famous historical site, or in a popular destination, such as New York City or Washington DC, your home can be fairly simple, yet still do well as a B&B.
transcript.translation: 如果你住在著名的历史遗址附近，或热门目的地，如纽约市或华盛顿特区，你的家可以相当简单，但作为住宿加早餐仍然能经营得很好。

transcript.text: On the other hand, if your home is architecturally unique, or has facilities for the traveler, such as a private entrance, private bath, or swimming pool, people may be willing to go some distance to reach you.
transcript.translation: 另一方面，如果你的家在建筑上独特，或有旅行者设施，如私人入口、私人浴室或游泳池，人们可能愿意长途跋涉来你这里。

transcript.text: Another important factor is the lifestyle of you and your family.
transcript.translation: 另一个重要因素是你和你家人的生活方式。

transcript.text: You must take into account whether all members of the family truly enjoy visitors, want to repeatedly discuss local sites and activities, and have the time and energy to handle the additional cooking, cleaning, laundry, and bookkeeping involved.
transcript.translation: 你必须考虑家庭成员是否真正喜欢访客，是否愿意反复讨论当地景点和活动，以及是否有时间和精力处理额外的烹饪、清洁、洗衣和簿记工作。

transcript.text: The final consideration is a financial one.
transcript.translation: 最后一个考虑因素是财务方面。

transcript.text: Potential B&B hosts must be realistic about opportunities for income.
transcript.translation: 潜在的住宿加早餐房东必须对收入机会持现实态度。

transcript.text: While B&Bs usually have low initial costs, experts estimate it would take at least five rooms rented regularly for the host to earn a living from B&B.
transcript.translation: 虽然住宿加早餐通常初始成本较低，但专家估计，房东至少需要定期出租五个房间才能从中谋生。

paragraphs.text: By now, it is generally accepted that regular exercise comes with an assortment of health benefits for people who maintain the habit over time. But is it __26__ too late to start?

paragraphs.text: New research looked at people who increased their exercise levels after their 40s beyond levels they had when they were younger and those individuals showed declines in their risk of early __27__ which were similar to those of people who exercised consistently throughout their lives. This was a __28__ of 32% to 35% compared to people who did not exercise. Those who began exercising in middle age also saw reductions in their incidence of __29__ diseases, such as heart disease and cancer, which were similar to the steady exercisers.
paragraphs.translation: 新研究考察了那些在40岁后增加锻炼水平、超过年轻时水平的人，这些人早逝风险的降低程度与终身坚持锻炼的人相似。与不锻炼的人相比，这相当于下降了32%至35%。那些中年开始锻炼的人，其慢性病（如心脏病和癌症）的发病率也出现了类似持续锻炼者的减少。

paragraphs.text: So why bother exercising consistently throughout your life? The authors of the study __30__ that some might interpret the study's findings to mean that they can delay starting an exercise program, but this would be a mistake. There are other benefits, both mental and physical, to staying consistently active that we should not __31__. These real health benefits include better __32__ functioning and lowered risk of gaining weight. The latter is __33__ important given the global obesity epidemic. In addition, experts assert that starting younger is better because, if you make a habit of exercising when you are young, you are more likely to keep up those __34__ later in life. It is ideal, then, for people to start exercising when they are children or __35__, and it is good to maintain an active lifestyle at all times regardless of your age. However, this study does indicate that, if you have not been active, you can still benefit if you start becoming active in your 40s and 50s.
paragraphs.translation: 那么，为何要终身坚持锻炼呢？该研究的作者承认，有些人可能将研究结果理解为可以推迟开始锻炼计划，但这将是错误的。坚持持续活跃还有其他身心益处，我们不应忽视。这些真实的健康益处包括认知功能改善和降低体重增加的风险。鉴于全球肥胖流行，后者尤为重要。此外，专家强调，年轻时开始锻炼更好，因为如果你在年轻时养成锻炼习惯，更可能在晚年保持这些模式。因此，理想情况是人们在儿童或青少年时期开始锻炼，并且无论年龄如何，都应始终保持积极的生活方式。然而，这项研究确实表明，如果你之前不活跃，在40多岁和50多岁开始活跃起来，仍然可以受益。

questionGroups.title: Restaurants are now employing robots — should chefs be worried?

material.title: Restaurants are now employing robots — should chefs be worried?

paragraphs.text: Like most chefs, Flippy is not afraid of hard work. Since last summer, that has meant 11am until 7pm shifts at Caliburger in Pasadena, California, as well as short assignments at Chick-N-Tots at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. These are long hours of repetitive work, where the boss demands absolute consistency. But you won't hear Flippy complain or say anything, in fact. For Flippy is a robot — a cloud-connected mechanical arm with 3D thermal scanners for eyes — that can flip burgers or fry 80 baskets of food an hour, monitor that food and even clean up afterwards.
paragraphs.translation: 像大多数厨师一样，Flippy 不惧怕辛勤工作。自去年夏天以来，这意味着每天在加州帕萨迪纳的 Caliburger 从早上11点工作到晚上7点，以及在洛杉矶道奇体育场的 Chick-N-Tots 承担短期任务。这些都是长时间的重复性工作，老板要求绝对的一致性。但你不会听到 Flippy 抱怨或说任何话，事实上。因为 Flippy 是一个机器人——一个云连接的机械臂，以用于视觉的 3D 热扫描仪作为“眼睛”——它可以翻转汉堡或每小时煎炸 80 篮食物，监控食物，甚至事后清理。

paragraphs.text: Flippy was created by Miso Robotics, part of the Cali Group, which is described by its CEO, John Miller, as: "A technology company that happens to sell cheeseburgers." Cali creates new machines that it road-tests in its Caliburger restaurants across the world, into which Flippy will be deployed this year. And Flippy is not alone. Also in California, Bear Robotics has developed a self-guiding robot, Penny, which has so far served 40,000 diners.
paragraphs.translation: Flippy 由 Miso Robotics 创造，该公司是 Cali Group 的一部分。其首席执行官约翰·米勒将其描述为：“一家碰巧卖芝士汉堡的科技公司。”Cali 创造新机器，并在其全球的 Caliburger 餐厅进行实地测试，Flippy 将于今年部署到这些餐厅。而 Flippy 并非孤例。同样在加州，Bear Robotics 开发了一种自主引导机器人 Penny，迄今为止已为 40,000 名顾客提供服务。

paragraphs.text: Ten years ago, robot-chefs and waiters were pure science fiction. Today, they are a reality, and at prices that make them a plausible investment. From May, Penny will be shipped on a subscription basis that offers "an immediate return", says Bear Robotics' chief operating officer, Juan Higueros. Flippy will cost a reported $60,000 to $100,000. Fully automated burger restaurants managed with minimal human oversight — where customers order at screens, pay electronically and eat food cooked and delivered by robots — are now a possibility.
paragraphs.translation: 十年前，机器人厨师和服务员纯粹是科幻小说。如今，它们已成为现实，并且价格使其成为一项看似合理的投资。Bear Robotics 的首席运营官胡安·伊格罗表示，从五月起，Penny 将以提供“即时回报”的订阅模式发货。据报道，Flippy 的成本在 60,000 到 100,000 美元之间。在最少人工监督下运营的全自动化汉堡餐厅——顾客在屏幕上点餐、电子支付、食用由机器人烹饪和递送的食物——现在已成为可能。

paragraphs.text: The technology exists, it just needs knitting together cost-effectively and in a way diners buy into. In an industry keen to slash labour costs and increase profits, further automation seems inevitable. After an eight-month test at Kang Nam Tofu House in California, Bear Robotics credited Penny with driving a 28% increase in sales. Meanwhile, in US trials, the self-ordering screens that McDonald's is currently installing at its 1,300 UK restaurants yielded a reported 30% rise in order values.
paragraphs.translation: 技术是存在的，只需要以成本效益高且顾客接受的方式将其整合在一起。在一个渴望削减劳动力成本、增加利润的行业中，进一步的自动化似乎是不可避免的。在加州 Kang Nam Tofu House 进行了八个月的测试后，Bear Robotics 将销售额增长 28% 归功于 Penny。与此同时，在美国的试验中，麦当劳目前在其 1,300 家英国餐厅安装的自助点餐屏幕据报道带来了 30% 的订单价值提升。

paragraphs.text: Personalisation is seen as key to the appeal of this technology, alongside its ability to reliably push so-called "upsells" (meal deals, extras, larger drinks) to customers. Soon when you log into a restaurant app, it will be able to use your data and purchasing history to recommend dishes to you — factoring in everything from the weather to, if you are ordering at a screen that can read your face, your mood.
paragraphs.translation: 个性化被视为这项技术吸引力的关键，同时还有其可靠地向顾客推销所谓“追加销售”（套餐、额外项目、大杯饮料）的能力。很快，当你登录一个餐厅应用时，它将能够利用你的数据和购买历史为你推荐菜品——考虑到从天气到，如果你在一个能识别人脸的屏幕上点餐，你的情绪等所有因素。

paragraphs.text: "Right now people compromise on choice. We're presented with a one-size-fits-all menu. Ultimately, technology can allow us to make personal choices. You love spicy food and chicken? Here's the dish people like you mostly order," says Tom Weaver, CEO at the hospitality tech company Flyt. He talks enthusiastically about the Helsinki pop-up Take-In, a full-service restaurant where diners ordered dishes in from various delivery services. "For the first time in a few hundred years, digital is allowing us to create new versions of restaurants."
paragraphs.translation: “现在人们在选择上做出妥协。我们面对的是千篇一律的菜单。最终，技术可以让我们做出个性化选择。你喜欢辛辣食物和鸡肉？这是像你这样的人最常点的菜，”餐饮科技公司 Flyt 的首席执行官汤姆·韦弗说。他热情地谈论了赫尔辛基的快闪餐厅 Take-In，这是一个全方位服务的餐厅，顾客在那里从各种送餐服务中点菜。“几百年来第一次，数字化让我们能够创造新形式的餐厅。”

paragraphs.text: If high-street fast food is automation-ready, its impact on high-end restaurants is likely to be subtler and slower. "It'll probably be a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef," says Noel Sharkey, professor of AI and robotics at the University of Sheffield. "Apart from the AI creativity gap, great cooking involves a subtle understanding of ingredients and delicate cooking that would be enormously challenging for robots. Placing fragile foods on plates would be incredibly slow."
paragraphs.translation: 如果街头快餐已准备好迎接自动化，那么它对高端餐厅的影响可能更为微妙和缓慢。“我们可能还要等很久才能看到五星级的机器人厨师，”谢菲尔德大学人工智能和机器人学教授诺埃尔·夏基说。“除了人工智能创造力的差距，烹饪涉及对食材微妙的理解和精细的烹饪，这对机器人来说将是巨大的挑战。将易碎食物放到盘子上将会极其缓慢。”

paragraphs.text: Currently, robots have limited functionality. A human needs to load Penny with plates that diners lift off themselves. At the robot-powered US pizza-delivery company Zume, the more difficult jobs, such as topping pizzas, are still done by humans. But Moley, which will launch soon, offers an idea of the sophistication to come. Modelled on the movements of a MasterChef contest winner, Tim Anderson, its robotic arms are fixed over a stove and programmed to prepare dishes from raw ingredients. It is designed for domestic use, but a commercial version is planned that opens up the possibility of restaurant kitchens automating even highly technically challenging tasks.
paragraphs.translation: 目前，机器人的功能有限。需要人工将盘子装到 Penny 上，由用餐者自行取下。在机器人驱动的美国披萨外卖公司 Zume，更困难的工作，如给披萨加配料，仍然由人工完成。但即将推出的 Moley 提供了一个关于未来精密程度的构想。其机械臂模仿了《厨艺大师》比赛冠军蒂姆·安德森的动作，固定在炉灶上方，并被编程为从原始食材开始准备菜肴。它是为家庭使用设计的，但计划推出商业版本，这为餐厅厨房自动化甚至技术难度很高的任务开辟了可能性。

paragraphs.text: For now, the kitchen technology that QSR Automations supplies to Mitchells & Butlers' pubs or KFC is less glamorous. Rather than having a chef shouting out diners' orders, the QSR system automatically distributes those orders across screens. The kitchen screens then tell chefs when to start cooking each dish, so that your plate of fish, chips and peas comes together at the right time.
paragraphs.translation: 目前，QSR Automations 供应给 Mitchells & Butlers 旗下的酒吧或肯德基的厨房技术没那么吸引人。QSR 系统不是让厨师喊出顾客的订单，而是自动将这些订单分配到各个屏幕上。然后厨房屏幕会告诉厨师何时开始烹饪每道菜，这样你的鱼、薯条和豌豆就能在正确的时间一起上桌。

paragraphs.text: The restaurant industry is currently suffering a severe shortage of skilled chefs — a deficit of 11,000, according to the skills agency People 1st. "Automation systems designed to make the process more idiot-proof are trying to bridge that gap," says Stefan Chomka, the editor of Restaurant magazine.
paragraphs.translation: 目前，餐饮业正严重缺乏熟练厨师——根据技能机构 People 1st 的数据，缺口达 11,000 人。“旨在让流程更不容易出错的自动化系统，正试图弥补这一差距，”《餐厅》杂志编辑斯特凡·乔姆卡说。

paragraphs.text: In terms of simplifying or enhancing the customer experience, online restaurant booking has been the easily-won success of the internet age. Automated at-table ordering and payment is seen as the next landmark. Until then, early adopters, such as the Manchester bar owner Andy Smith, who uses the Ordoo app at his venue 33 Oldham Street, may well experience growing but "lower than expected" acceptance.
paragraphs.translation: 在简化或提升顾客体验方面，在线餐厅预订是互联网时代轻易取得的成功。自动化餐桌点餐和支付被视为下一个里程碑。在此之前，像曼彻斯特酒吧老板安迪·史密斯这样的早期采用者——他在自己的场所 33 Oldham Street 使用 Ordoo 应用——可能会经历增长但“低于预期”的接受度。

paragraphs.text: Embarrassing failures in restaurant tech frequently hit the headlines. The TGI Fridays drone that injured a Brooklyn Daily photographer; US burger chain Shake Shack having to retreat from plans for entirely cashless ordering sites. But, says Chomka, such technology could miss the mark if it only offers "solutions to problems that don't really exist". "Payments being automatic" could be useful, he adds. But, in an expensive restaurant, "how quick do you need dinner to be?"
paragraphs.translation: 餐饮科技领域的尴尬失败经常登上头条。TGI Fridays 的无人机伤到了《布鲁克林每日新闻》的摄影师；美国汉堡连锁店 Shake Shack 不得不放弃完全无现金点餐点的计划。但是，乔姆卡说，如果此类技术只提供“对并不存在的问题的解决方案”，它可能无法切中要害。“自动支付”可能是有用的，他补充道。但是，在昂贵的餐厅里，“你需要晚餐有多快？”

paragraphs.text: That attachment to the human art of hospitality will be heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs. "Unite is concerned that without safeguards, any benefits will bypass workers in low-paying jobs, such as waiters," says the union's London regional officer, Dave Turnbull. "We're urging Members of Parliament to ensure automation does not just benefit a wealthy few like previous industrial revolutions."
paragraphs.translation: 对人性化待客艺术的这种依恋，对将自动化视为就业威胁的员工来说将是令人欣慰的。“联合工会担心，如果没有保障措施，任何好处都将绕过像服务员这样的低薪工作者，”该工会的伦敦地区官员戴夫·特恩布尔说。“我们敦促议员们确保自动化不仅仅像之前的工业革命那样让少数富人受益。”

paragraphs.text: The industry principle is that automation will allow it to redeploy staff more effectively. Jobs will change, if not immediately decrease in number. "Self-order screens mean more demand for people front-of-house. Last year, we recruited 1,000 new managers," says McDonald's COO, Jason Clark. Caliburger has a programme to retrain staff as robot engineers or "chef techs".
paragraphs.translation: 行业原则是，自动化将使其能够更有效地重新部署员工。工作岗位将会改变，即使数量不会立即减少。“自助点餐屏幕意味着对前台人员的需求增加。去年，我们招聘了 1,000 名新经理，”麦当劳首席运营官杰森·克拉克说。Caliburger 有一个将员工再培训为机器人工程师或“厨师技术员”的计划。

paragraphs.text: But ultimately the chance to reduce overheads by employing fewer people or at lower rates will be what attracts big brands to technology. Invariably, over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants, not least because automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery. Companies such as Domino and Just Eat have both experimented with robot and drone delivery, which is already legal in Reykjavik, Iceland. "Robot food deliveries are the future," says Noel Sharkey. "Small, 4mph ground robots are safe and will work 24 hours a day."
paragraphs.translation: 但最终，通过雇用更少的人或以更低工资雇用来降低管理费用的机会，将是吸引大品牌采用技术的因素。不可避免地，在未来 10 年，传统的实体餐厅将会失去工作岗位，尤其是因为自动化将推动其快速增长的竞争对手：外卖。Domino 和 Just Eat 等公司都试验过机器人和无人机送货，这在冰岛雷克雅维克已经是合法的。“机器人送餐是未来，”诺埃尔·夏基说。“小型、时速 4 英里的地面机器人是安全的，并且可以全天候工作。”

paragraphs.text: Combined with machine learning of anticipated order volumes and the minute-by-minute cooking data generated by systems such as QSR, that robot fleet could deliver almost instantly. "Restaurants will prepare food ahead of orders coming in," predicts Just Eat's director of engineering, Daniel Richardson. "I'll be able to say 'Let's have pizza' to my family, my intelligent assistant will hear and 10 minutes later the food will be at my door." No one is putting an exact date on it yet. But in the dining room and on your doorstep, the robots are coming.
paragraphs.translation: 结合对预期订单量的机器学习以及 QSR 等系统产生的逐分钟烹饪数据，这个机器人车队几乎可以即时送货。“餐厅将在订单到来之前准备好食物，”Just Eat 的工程总监丹尼尔·理查森预测。“我可以对家人说‘我们吃披萨吧’，我的智能助手会听到，10 分钟后食物就会送到我的门口。”目前还没有人确定具体的日期。但在餐厅和你家门口，机器人正在到来。

questionGroups.directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.

questions.statementText: It is now possible to fully automate a burger restaurant with little human supervision.
questions.analysis: C段末尾明确指出："Fully automated burger restaurants managed with minimal human oversight... are now a possibility." 题目中的"little human supervision"对应原文的"minimal human oversight"。

questions.statementText: At a robot-powered US company, complicated tasks still have to be performed by humans.
questions.analysis: H段提到在机器人驱动的美国披萨外卖公司Zume，"the more difficult jobs, such as topping pizzas, are still done by humans"，题目中的"complicated tasks"对应原文的"more difficult jobs"。

questions.statementText: More automation appears to be a certainty in industries eager to cut labour costs and raise profits.
questions.analysis: D段指出："In an industry keen to slash labour costs and increase profits, further automation seems inevitable." 题目中的"a certainty"对应原文的"inevitable"，"cut labour costs and raise profits"对应"slash labour costs and increase profits"。

questions.statementText: There are often front-page reports of failures in technological innovation of the restaurant industry.
questions.analysis: L段开头提到："Embarrassing failures in restaurant tech frequently hit the headlines." 题目中的"front-page reports"对应原文的"hit the headlines"，"often"对应"frequently"。

questions.statementText: Robot-chef Flippy does not fear laborious work, nor does it make any complaints.
questions.analysis: A段开头说"Flippy is not afraid of hard work"，后文又说"you won't hear Flippy complain"。题目中的"laborious work"对应"hard work"，"nor does it make any complaints"对应"won't hear Flippy complain"。

questions.statementText: Digital technology makes it possible for businesses to innovate restaurant models.
questions.analysis: F段末尾引用Tom Weaver的话："digital is allowing us to create new versions of restaurants." 题目中的"innovate restaurant models"对应原文的"create new versions of restaurants"。

questions.statementText: Fondness for human warmth in catering to customers will give hope to employees who are afraid of losing jobs to robots.
questions.analysis: M段开头说："That attachment to the human art of hospitality will be heartening for staff who see automation as a threat to jobs." 题目中的"fondness for human warmth"对应"attachment to the human art of hospitality"，"give hope"对应"heartening"。

questions.statementText: There is an acute shortage of experienced chefs in the catering industry and automated cooking is expected to fill the gap.
questions.analysis: J段指出餐饮业"suffering a severe shortage of skilled chefs"，并引用编辑的话说自动化系统"are trying to bridge that gap"。题目中的"acute shortage"对应"severe shortage"，"fill the gap"对应"bridge that gap"。

questions.statementText: Over the coming decade, many jobs in traditional restaurants will disappear due to robot delivery.
questions.analysis: O段提到："over the next 10 years, jobs will go in conventional bricks-built restaurants, not least because automation will boost their rapidly growing rival: delivery." 题目中的"coming decade"对应"next 10 years"，"traditional restaurants"对应"conventional bricks-built restaurants"。

questions.statementText: According to an expert in AI and robotics, it may be quite some time before a master robot-chef appears.
questions.analysis: G段引用谢菲尔德大学AI与机器人学教授Noel Sharkey的话："It'll probably be a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef." 题目中的"quite some time"对应"a very long time"，"a master robot-chef"对应"a five-star robot-chef"。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in. However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.
paragraphs.translation: 许多人将友谊视为安慰之毯：可以依靠哭泣的肩膀，一个可靠的倾诉对象。然而，往往在我们热切追求个人成功的过程中，我们失去了朋友，而这已经成为过程的一部分。

paragraphs.text: The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships. As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones.
paragraphs.translation: 伴随日常生活的混乱和永无休止的动荡，是追求稳定友谊的严重障碍。作为学生，我们用这个借口来推卸失去那些我们曾认为是所爱之人的责任。

paragraphs.text: Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track. We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.
paragraphs.translation: 我们不应将生活视为一场竞赛，每个人都在通往某种成功的道路上独行，而必须重新学会珍视沿途建立的联系。我们必须重新评估激进的个人自由所带来的危害。

paragraphs.text: Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective. It argues, for instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatened the dream of many Americans.
paragraphs.translation: 激进的个人主义将个人的自由置于集体之上。例如，它认为全民医疗保健——集体主义的一个例子——威胁了许多美国人的梦想。

paragraphs.text: Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture. Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.
paragraphs.translation: 我们许多人都成为了个人主义文化的受害者。社会倾向于庆祝个人成就，并基于这样一种假设来赞扬它：获胜或成功是比他人更努力工作的结果。

paragraphs.text: As a society, we idolize the concept of "losing friends on the road to success." I remember hearing in high school, "Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college. That's all that will matter in the long run," a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It's preached in many success stories, and it's embedded in the way we see growth. Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.
paragraphs.translation: 作为一个社会，我们崇拜“在成功之路上失去朋友”的概念。我记得在高中时听到过这样的说法：“别担心失去友谊，只需专注于学习和考上大学。从长远来看，这才是最重要的。”这种情绪并非我个人经历独有。它在许多成功故事中被宣扬，并深深植根于我们看待成长的方式中。励志演说家会推动他们的受众对失去朋友的必然结局安之若素。花太多时间与朋友在一起？你正在浪费本可用于成就的时间。投资于人际关系？不如投资于你的工作。

paragraphs.text: This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives. We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades. In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized.
paragraphs.translation: 这种不断追求成功的需要，使我们无法看透伴随日常生活的变革漩涡。我们被期望切实地取得成功，赢得奖项，获得更高的职位，取得更好的成绩。为了成功，我们失去了朋友，而可悲的是，这已经变得常态化。

paragraphs.text: We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors.
paragraphs.translation: 我们不能对失去友谊安之若素，因为它们是我们的精神支柱。

paragraphs.text: Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.
paragraphs.translation: 是的，追求成功。挑战自己。突破极限。但与所有自诩的成功专家相反，独自去做并不会让你比那些在他人帮助下取得成功的人更成功或更优秀。

paragraphs.text: Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else. Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.
paragraphs.translation: 努力培养健康的人际关系，并在似乎没有时间顾及他人的繁忙日程中维持它们。尽管我们可能生活在一个珍视独立追求成就的社会中，但在过程中有人支持和爱你，远比任何最终结果都重要。

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C), and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What often happens when people are eager to pursue individual success?

options.label: A
options.text: They lack a shoulder to cry on.

options.label: B
options.text: They have no soul to confide in.

options.label: C
options.text: They cannot find reliable friends.

options.label: D
options.text: They ignore their ties with friends.

questions.analysis: 文章第一段明确指出："in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process." 在追求个人成功的过程中，我们失去了朋友，这说明人们忽视了与朋友的联系。D选项"忽视与朋友的关系"准确概括了这一现象。
questions.keySentence: However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.

wrongOptions.A: "缺少可以依靠的肩膀"是文章开头描述友谊价值的比喻，不是追求成功时发生的事情。
wrongOptions.B: "没有可以倾诉的人"同样只是第一段描述友谊功能的内容，不是追求成功的后果。
wrongOptions.C: 文章说的是"失去朋友"而非"找不到可靠的朋友"，且原因是自己的忽视，而非客观上找不到。

questions.questionText: What does the author advise people to do in their pursuit of radical individualism?

options.label: A
options.text: Reexamine its detrimental effects.

options.label: B
options.text: Shrug off the loss of their loved ones.

options.label: C
options.text: Avoid the chaos and turmoil involved.

options.label: D
options.text: Remove aggressive obstacles in the way.

questions.analysis: 第三段作者建议："We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom." reevaluate the harm意为"重新评估其危害"，与A选项"重新审视其有害影响"(reexamine its detrimental effects)含义一致。detrimental effects对应harm，reexamine对应reevaluate。
questions.keySentence: We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.

wrongOptions.B: "对失去亲友不以为意"与作者观点相反，作者认为我们不应忽视友谊的丧失。
wrongOptions.C: "避免混乱和动荡"是第二段提到的日常生活特征，不是作者给出的建议。
wrongOptions.D: "移除障碍"是对第二段内容的曲解，作者并未建议人们去移除障碍。

questions.questionText: What is American society's assumption of personal achievement?

options.label: A
options.text: It is to be duly celebrated and highly commended.

options.label: B
options.text: It is a sure way to fulfill a person's dream.

options.label: C
options.text: It revolves around an individualistic culture.

options.label: D
options.text: It reflects a person's exceptional endeavor.

questions.analysis: 第五段指出："Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person." 社会的假设是成功是比别人更努力工作的结果，即个人成就反映了个人的超凡努力。D选项中的"exceptional endeavor"（杰出的努力）对应"working harder than the next person"。
questions.keySentence: Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.

wrongOptions.A: "应当被庆祝和赞扬"是社会对个人成就的态度，而非对个人成就的假设(assumption)，混淆了态度和假设。
wrongOptions.B: 文章未提及个人成就是实现梦想的可靠途径，这属于无中生有。
wrongOptions.C: 个人主义文化是背景，而非社会对个人成就本身的假设。

questions.questionText: What is preached in many success stories?

options.label: A
options.text: Attaching importance to academic gains on the road to success.

options.label: B
options.text: Investing one's time in work instead of connecting with friends.

options.label: C
options.text: Trying to strengthen friendships in one's pursuit of personal success.

options.label: D
options.text: Excelling in academic performance to get into a prestigious college.

questions.analysis: 第六段列举了成功故事中宣扬的观点："Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead." 以及"Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements." 这些都在宣扬把时间投入工作而非维系友谊，与B选项一致。
questions.keySentence: Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.

wrongOptions.A: "重视学术成果"虽然第六段提到了学习和升学，但这只是一个例子，不是成功故事宣扬的核心内容。
wrongOptions.C: "努力在追求成功时加强友谊"与文章观点相反，文章说的是成功故事让人放弃友谊。
wrongOptions.D: "优异学业表现考入名校"只是第六段中一个高中时的具体例子，不是成功故事普遍宣扬的理念。

questions.questionText: What can we infer from the passage regarding the pursuit of success?

options.label: A
options.text: No one can succeed without pushing limits.

options.label: B
options.text: No one can afford to neglect close friends.

options.label: C
options.text: Collectivism is superior to individualism.

options.label: D
options.text: Success experts often lead people to ruin.

questions.analysis: 文章最后两段强调："We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors"以及"having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result." 全文主旨就是不能为了追求成功而忽视友谊，因此可以推断出没有人能承受忽视亲密朋友的代价。
questions.keySentence: Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else.

wrongOptions.A: "没有人能不突破极限就成功"过度推断，文章虽提到push limits，但这只是鼓励性话语，不是文章的推论。
wrongOptions.C: 文章并未主张集体主义优于个人主义，只是批评极端个人主义对友谊的伤害。
wrongOptions.D: 文章虽然批评了所谓的成功专家，但并未说他们会导致人们走向毁灭，这一说法过于极端。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace Prize, Martin Luther King Jr. said, "I believe that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word in reality."
paragraphs.translation: 在马丁·路德·金接受诺贝尔和平奖的演讲中，他说道：“我相信，赤裸的真理和无条件的爱将在现实中拥有最终的发言权。”

paragraphs.text: More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction. From disputes over the climate change to debates about how slavery is taught, America is at a crossroads. And the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations.
paragraphs.translation: 五十多年过去了，我们的社会仍在努力区分真理与幻想、事实与虚构。从气候变化的争议到奴隶制教学方式的辩论，美国正处于十字路口。而争取公平的斗争是这些关键对话的核心。

paragraphs.text: Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences. A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90-$113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.
paragraphs.translation: 一项又一项研究表明，不平等已经产生了可怕的后果。花旗集团2020年的一份报告指出，如果过去二十年中与高等教育相关的公平问题得到充分解决，“黑人学生的终身收入本可增加900亿至1130亿美元”。

paragraphs.text: This statistic represents a flood of issues we've failed to confront as a nation. It also highlights one truth: We're missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us. However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.
paragraphs.translation: 这一统计数据代表着我们作为一个国家未能面对的大量问题。它也凸显了一个事实：我们正在错失弥合分歧的宝贵机会。然而，通过纪念金的遗产，我们可以让国家回归真正公平的道路。

paragraphs.text: Students — and adults for that matter — simply cannot understand the conflicts we have today without understanding what caused them in the first place. That means we have a responsibility to help them make connections between U.S. history and current events. It also means giving them the tools they need to address inequity and bias in their own lives. Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we've come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel.
paragraphs.translation: 学生——以及成年人——如果不了解当前冲突的根本原因，就根本无法理解这些冲突。这意味着我们有责任帮助他们将美国历史与当前事件联系起来。这也意味着为他们提供工具，以应对自己生活中的不平等和偏见。坚持这些原则，加上对真诚对话的承诺，可以帮助每个学生更好地理解我们已取得的进步，并更清晰地看到我们仍需前行的道路。

paragraphs.text: With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country.
paragraphs.translation: 通过对需要更多合格、多样化教育工作者的更真实分析，我们可以改进全国学校的招聘、培训和留任策略。

paragraphs.text: Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements. A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before". But reports of increased polarization shouldn't persuade us to look away from one another. Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on.
paragraphs.translation: 不幸的是，我们根深蒂固的分歧正在延迟这些进步。最近的一项调查发现，77%的美国人认为国家“比以往任何时候都更加分裂”。但有关两极分化的报告不应说服我们彼此回避。相反，它们应迫使我们直面共同的问题。

paragraphs.text: We are not, as some would suggest, living in a "post-racial society". We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity. Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us. But our children and our grandchildren deserve better.
paragraphs.translation: 我们并非如一些人所暗示的，生活在一个“后种族社会”。在涉及种族不平等时，我们根本不能继续将头埋在沙子里。除非我们诚实面对不容忍、偏见以及这些社会疾病如何影响我们彼此相处的方式，否则不公正将继续困扰我们。但我们的子孙后代值得更好的未来。

paragraphs.text: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo. Let's continue to build a better, more inclusive nation; and in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."
paragraphs.translation: 在这个马丁·路德·金日及以后，让我们承诺共同努力打破现状。让我们继续建设一个更好、更包容的国家；用马丁·路德·金的话说，“一个与自身和平相处的社会，一个能与其良知共存的社会。”

questionGroups.directions: There are 2 passages in this section. Each passage is followed by some questions or unfinished statements. For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C), and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2 with a single line through the centre.

questions.questionText: What does the author think about today's America?

options.label: A
options.text: It is struggling to transform fiction into reality.

options.label: B
options.text: It has been the focus of many vital conversations.

options.label: C
options.text: It still has a long way to go before equity can be truly realized.

options.label: D
options.text: It has got to a point where people disagree on nearly every issue.

questions.analysis: 文章第二段指出美国社会"still struggling to separate truth from fantasy"，并说"the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations"。第四段进一步提到"We're missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us"。全文主旨表明美国在实现真正公平方面仍有很长的路要走，C选项准确概括了作者的观点。
questions.keySentence: More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction.

wrongOptions.A: "挣扎着将虚构变为现实"曲解了原文"separate truth from fantasy"的含义，原文是说区分真相与幻想，而非将虚构变为现实。
wrongOptions.B: "成为许多重要对话的焦点"只是文中提到的一个事实，不是作者对当今美国的核心看法。
wrongOptions.D: "在几乎每个问题上都有分歧"过度夸大，文章虽提到分裂，但并未说在每个问题上都有分歧。

questions.questionText: What do we learn from the passage about black students in the past 20 years?

options.label: A
options.text: They have been unfairly treated regarding higher education.

options.label: B
options.text: They have been battling hard to address equity issues.

options.label: C
options.text: They have boosted their lifetime incomes by billions of dollars.

options.label: D
options.text: They have come to see the consequences of racial discrimination.

questions.analysis: 第三段引用2020年花旗报告指出：黑人学生本可以增加900-1130亿美元的终身收入，"if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades"。这说明过去20年间高等教育方面的公平问题未得到充分解决，即黑人学生在高等教育方面受到了不公平对待。
questions.keySentence: Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90-$113 billion if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades.

wrongOptions.B: 文章未提及黑人学生一直在为解决公平问题而奋斗，这属于无中生有。
wrongOptions.C: 报告使用的是虚拟语气"could have increased"，表示本可以增加但实际上没有，C选项理解为已经增加了，与原文相反。
wrongOptions.D: 文章未提到黑人学生认识到了种族歧视的后果，这一说法缺乏文本依据。

questions.questionText: How can Americans bridge the differences that divide them?

options.label: A
options.text: By dealing with the thorny issues confronting them.

options.label: B
options.text: By seizing every chance to enhance racial harmony.

options.label: C
options.text: By continuing to pursue Martin Luther King Jr.'s cause.

options.label: D
options.text: By striving to identify exceedingly valuable opportunities.

questions.analysis: 第四段明确指出："by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity." 通过继承马丁·路德·金的遗志，美国可以重回通往真正公平的道路。C选项"继续追求马丁·路德·金的事业"与原文"honoring King's legacy"含义一致。
questions.keySentence: However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.

wrongOptions.A: "处理棘手问题"虽然是文章后面提到的内容，但不是针对"弥合分歧"这一问题的直接回答。
wrongOptions.B: "抓住每个机会促进种族和谐"在文中没有对应表述，属于过度推断。
wrongOptions.D: "努力发现极有价值的机会"曲解了原文，文章说的是"missing out on valuable opportunities"，而非要去寻找机会。

questions.questionText: How do most Americans view America as a nation according to a recent survey?

options.label: A
options.text: It is compelled to address its historical social issues.

options.label: B
options.text: It is delaying advancements toward racial equality.

options.label: C
options.text: It has kept itself from polarization.

options.label: D
options.text: It has become increasingly split.

questions.analysis: 第七段明确引用调查数据："A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is 'more divided than ever before'." 77%的美国人认为国家比以往任何时候都更加分裂，D选项"变得越来越分裂"(increasingly split)准确对应"more divided than ever before"。
questions.keySentence: A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before".

wrongOptions.A: "被迫解决历史社会问题"是作者的观点，不是调查中大多数美国人的看法。
wrongOptions.B: "延缓种族平等的进步"是文章前一句的内容，不是调查结果所反映的美国人的看法。
wrongOptions.C: "避免了两极分化"与原文相反，调查显示美国人认为国家更加分裂而非避免了分裂。

questions.questionText: What does the author suggest Americans do?

options.label: A
options.text: Ensure the wellbeing of their children and grandchildren.

options.label: B
options.text: Make joint efforts to tackle the nation's equity issues.

options.label: C
options.text: Restrain their intolerance and discrimination.

options.label: D
options.text: Restore social order for a harmonious nation.

questions.analysis: 文章最后一段作者呼吁："let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo. Let's continue to build a better, more inclusive nation." 作者建议美国人共同努力打破现状，建设一个更好、更包容的国家。B选项"共同努力解决国家的公平问题"准确概括了作者的建议，working together对应make joint efforts。
questions.keySentence: On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo.

wrongOptions.A: "确保子孙后代的福祉"虽然文中提到"our children and our grandchildren deserve better"，但这是论证的理由，不是作者的核心建议。
wrongOptions.C: "克制不宽容和歧视"只是作者提到的一个方面，不足以概括作者的整体建议。
wrongOptions.D: "恢复社会秩序以建设和谐国家"的表述过于笼统，且文中未使用"restore social order"的概念。

questionGroups.sourceText: 尊老是中华民族的传统美德，深深植根于中国人的思想和行为中，是人们普遍遵守的行为规范和社会准则。在当今的中国，这种美德得到广泛传承。社会各界积极营造敬老助老的社会氛围。为老年人提供便利服务已成为社会共识，例如社区专门开设长者食堂，公共场所配置优先座位。政府还出台了一系列政策，为老年人的权益提供有力保障。尊老是社会和谐与发展的重要基石，有助于培育良好的社会氛围，推动整个社会文明进步。

answer.model_translation: Respecting the elderly is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation, deeply rooted in the thoughts and behaviors of the Chinese people. It is a widely observed code of conduct and social norm. In today's China, this virtue has been extensively passed down. All sectors of society actively foster a social atmosphere of respecting and assisting the elderly. Providing convenient services for senior citizens has become a social consensus. For example, communities have set up canteens specifically for the elderly, and public places are equipped with priority seating. The government has also introduced a series of policies to provide strong protection for the rights and interests of the elderly. Respecting the elderly serves as an important cornerstone of social harmony and development, contributing to the cultivation of a positive social atmosphere and promoting the progress of civilization across society as a whole.
answer.translation_analysis: 本段翻译采用了以下策略：1）四字格及中文特色表达的意译处理，如"传统美德"译为 traditional virtue，"行为规范和社会准则"译为 code of conduct and social norm，准确传达含义的同时符合英文表达习惯；2）长句拆分，将原文中较长的复合句拆分为多个短句，使英文表达更加清晰流畅；3）被动语态的灵活运用，如"深深植根于"译为 deeply rooted in，"得到广泛传承"译为 has been extensively passed down，符合英语学术文体特点；4）抽象概念的具体化处理，如"社会各界"译为 all sectors of society，"社会共识"译为 social consensus；5）举例部分使用 for example 自然衔接，保持原文的论证逻辑。
